content:
Bookstore Leave Behind ('留下書舍'), which is caught up in a national security case and has been suspended for over a month, announced today (the 25th) that it will proceed with its original plan to close down after the 30th of August. The bookstore will resume its final operations for five consecutive days from tomorrow (the 26th) to Sunday (the 30th), opening from 1pm to 9pm daily for a clearance sale.

Leave Behind Bookstore posted closing remarks on social media, stating: 'Four years pass in a snap; flowers fall yet we remain friends of the mind. In books there is no golden house, nor a beauty fair as jade. Why force the will of a lifetime? Boiling wine in cheerful talk is enough. Tears fall at this final note, I know not what to say—only a word of thanks. Take care.'

Opened for four years, Leave Behind Bookstore announced last month that it would close at the end of August. A day later, national security police officers visited and arrested three people from the bookstore on suspicion of committing the offence of sedition under Article 23. Two people from Tin Tin Books ('田園書屋') were arrested in the same case. Tin Tin Books, with a 50-year history, also announced at the end of last month that it would close once its lease expired. The publication in question is reported to be 'Red Flowers Bloom: Identity and Belonging in the Era of Xi Jinping', written by Chinese-American journalist Eve Lee ('馮哲芸').

Leave Behind Bookstore was founded in 2022 by veteran media person Shum Wan-wah ('岑蘊華') and several former Stand News ('立場新聞') reporters. At the time, Apple Daily ('蘋果日報'), Stand News, and Citizen News ('眾新聞') had already ceased operations one after another. The name 'Leave Behind' and 'Bookstore' symbolises 'leaving writing behind'. The bookstore focuses on books related to news reporting and the media, and also regularly hosts talks and author sharing sessions.

On the 14th of last month, Leave Behind Bookstore announced that it would close on the 30th of August, stating that the unpredictable 'red line' was also a reason for the closure.
